## 1. System & Security

### OS, Kernel & Patch State
- **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Noble Numbat), x86_64. **Kernel:** `6.8.0-106-generic` (built 2026-03-06).
- **Install age:** Root filesystem created **2026-02-09** (~4 months old). `wtmp` history begins 2026-03-04.
- **Uptime:** 37 days (booted ~2026-05-03).
- **Timezone:** `Europe/Berlin` (CEST, +0200). NTP active, clock synchronized. **Locale:** `C.UTF-8` throughout.
- **REBOOT REQUIRED — flagged.** `/var/run/reboot-required` is present. Four newer kernels are installed and pending (`6.8.0-110/111/117/124`) plus `linux-base`. The running kernel `-106` is **18 builds behind** the latest installed `-124`. The box has not rebooted into patched kernels for 37 days. **Livepatch is NOT enabled** (machine is not attached to Ubuntu Pro), so these kernel CVEs are live until reboot.

### Package Management & Auto-Updates
- **913 packages** installed (`dpkg -l | grep ^ii`). **No held packages** (apt-mark / dpkg both clean).
- **unattended-upgrades 2.9.1** installed, **enabled + active**. `20auto-upgrades` has both `Update-Package-Lists "1"` and `Unattended-Upgrade "1"` set. Allowed-Origins = noble + noble-security (+ ESM origins, but ESM is unavailable without Pro). **`Automatic-Reboot` is NOT set** (commented out in default config) — this is why kernel updates pile up un-applied and the reboot-required flag persists. No `Automatic-Reboot-Time` either.
- **Recent apt activity is healthy and automated:** unattended-upgrade ran daily — e.g. 2026-06-09 upgraded `systemd` stack (255.4-1ubuntu8.14→8.16), `rsync`, `telnet`; 2026-06-05 `python3-twisted`, `urllib3`, `nano`. Last run 2026-06-09 06:15.
- **24 packages upgradable** (0 flagged as security-only in the standard pocket; remaining security fixes likely sit behind ESM which is not subscribed).
- **Ubuntu Pro: NOT attached.** ESM-infra/ESM-apps, Livepatch, and USG all available but inactive.

### Users & Privilege
- **No human (uid≥1000) login accounts.** uid≥1000 entries are all service accounts: `www` (1000, nologin), `mysql` (1001, nologin), `postgres` (1002, /bin/sh), `named` (1003, nologin).
- **Only two accounts with real shells:** `root` (/bin/bash) and `postgres` (/bin/sh, expected for PG).
- **Only `root` has a usable (unlocked) password hash** (`$y$` = yescrypt). All other entries in shadow are locked (`!`/`*`). 
- **Sudoers:** stock — `root`, `%sudo`, `%admin` get ALL. The `sudo`, `admin`, and `root` groups have **no extra members** (only root is implicitly privileged). One drop-in: `/etc/sudoers.d/90-cloud-init-users` grants `root ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL` (cloud-init default, low risk since root already is root).
- **Logins:** `last -n 15` shows only `root`, almost all from `127.0.0.1` (local pts, i.e. aaPanel terminal / tooling). Two real remote root logins on 2026-05-03 from `129.222.57.160` and `103.216.160.98`. **Nobody currently logged in** (`who` empty at scan time).

### SSH Hardening — WEAK (highest-priority issue)
Effective config (`sshd -T`):
- **Port 22** (default, not changed).
- **`PermitRootLogin yes`** — direct root SSH allowed.
- **`PasswordAuthentication yes`** — and this comes from a **drop-in conflict**: `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/50-cloud-init.conf` sets `yes` while `60-cloudimg-settings.conf` sets `no`. SSH applies **first-match-wins**, and `50-` sorts before `60-`, so **password auth is effectively ON** (confirmed by `sshd -T`). The intended hardening in the 60- file is silently overridden.
- `PubkeyAuthentication yes`, `KbdInteractiveAuthentication no`, `PermitEmptyPasswords no`, `MaxAuthTries 6`, `LoginGraceTime 120`, `UsePAM yes`. **No `AllowUsers`/`AllowGroups`/`DenyUsers`** restriction. `X11Forwarding yes` (unnecessary on a server).
- **Net effect: root can log in over SSH with a password** — the single most exploitable misconfiguration, given active brute-forcing (below).
- **`/root/.ssh/authorized_keys`** (perms `-rw------`, dir `0700` — correct): **4 ed25519 keys** — comments: `root@vmi3124690`, `claude-code`, `claude-code`, `vps-147.93.138.77-contabo`. (Two identical-comment `claude-code` keys — worth confirming both are intended.)

### Active Brute-Force Pressure (no fail2ban)
- **`fail2ban` is NOT installed** and there is no aaPanel SSH-jail daemon running.
- **SSH is under heavy active attack:** ~**12,360 failed/invalid SSH auth events today** (`journalctl -u ssh`). Top sources today: `102.203.197.6` (1066), `178.105.144.231` (717), `139.224.164.180` (468), `87.251.64.147` (459), `8.222.228.2` (409). `lastb` shows live username spraying (`root`, `frappe`, `steam`, `customer`, `teamspea`, `openclaw`) from `8.222.228.2`.
- **aaPanel ipset blacklist is EMPTY** (`aapanel.ipv4.blacklist` = 0 entries; whitelist also 0) — so the panel's own brute-force/auto-ban protection is effectively not catching these. **There is currently no automated SSH ban mechanism in place.** Combined with password+root SSH enabled, this is the top risk.

### Firewall — UFW active, but two world-open ports flagged
`ufw status verbose`: **active**, default `deny incoming` / `allow outgoing`. iptables shows aaPanel-managed chains layered on top (`aapanel.ipv4.blacklist` DROP + `whitelist` ACCEPT before UFW). Allowed-in (IPv4+IPv6, all from Anywhere):

| Port | Purpose | Actual bind | Real exposure |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20/21 tcp | pure-ftpd (FTP + data) | 0.0.0.0 | **Exposed** |
| 22 tcp | SSH | 0.0.0.0 | **Exposed (under attack)** |
| 80/443 tcp | nginx web | 0.0.0.0 | Exposed (expected) |
| 888 tcp | nginx (phpMyAdmin / default vhost) | 0.0.0.0 | **Exposed** |
| 10873 tcp | aaPanel admin UI (`webserver`/openresty) | 0.0.0.0 | **Exposed** |
| 39000-40000 tcp | FTP passive range | — | Exposed (FTP passive) |
| 5432 tcp/udp | **opened in UFW** | **127.0.0.1 only** | **NOT reachable** (Postgres binds loopback only — UFW rule is misleading/unnecessary but harmless) |
| 53 tcp/udp | PowerDNS authoritative | 0.0.0.0 | Exposed (intended, see below) |

**Cross-check finding (good news):** **MariaDB on :3306 binds 0.0.0.0 but 3306 is NOT in the UFW allow-list → blocked at firewall.** Likewise the app ports **3000/3001 (prod web/api) and 3002/3003 (staging web/api) bind 0.0.0.0/`*` but are NOT in UFW → blocked** (reachable only via nginx reverse proxy). So despite wide binds, the firewall correctly fences DB and app ports. **The one genuinely needless rule is 5432 open in UFW** (service is loopback-only) — close it to reduce confusion; no live exposure.

### PowerDNS (:53) — authoritative-only, NOT an open resolver (safe)
- `pdns_server` running as user `pdns`, `launch=bind`, serving zones from `/etc/powerdns/named.conf` / `/var/named/chroot`. This is **aaPanel's DNS Manager** authoritative server.
- **No recursion:** no `recursor`/`allow-recursion` directives; **no `pdns_recursor` process**. Self-test `dig @127.0.0.1 google.com` returned **NO answer and no `ra` (recursion-available) flag** → **confirmed NOT an open resolver**. Authoritative-only on :53 is acceptable exposure. `version-string=anonymous` set (good — hides version). No PowerDNS webserver/API enabled.

### pure-ftpd (:21) — running, hardened config, but plaintext-capable
- Active config `/www/server/pure-ftpd/etc/pure-ftpd.conf`: **`TLS 1`** (TLS *optional/allowed*, not enforced — value 2 would force it), TLS cert present at `/etc/ssl/private/pure-ftpd.pem`. `NoAnonymous yes`, `UnixAuthentication no`, `PureDB` virtual-user auth, `ChrootEveryone yes`, `MinUID 100`, passive `39000-40000`, max 50 clients.
- **Zero FTP virtual users** (`pureftpd.passwd`/`.pdb` empty) — so FTP currently has **no usable accounts**, but the daemon is still listening publicly. With TLS only optional, any future user could authenticate in cleartext. Since it's unused, consider stopping it / closing 20-21.

### Scheduled Work
- **Root crontab:** aaPanel hashed cron `…cdcccd82` (daily 01:50) + acme.sh renewal (daily 15:38). 
- **`/etc/cron.d` app automation (notable):** `lucifer-autodeploy` and `lucifer-staging-autodeploy` both run **every minute as root** via `/usr/local/bin/lucifer-*-autodeploy.sh`; `lucifer-staging-dbsync` runs daily 04:00 (prod→staging DB sync). These root-owned per-minute auto-deploy scripts are a notable supply-chain/privilege surface (anything that can write those scripts or the watched git ref gets root) — worth a content review.
- Stock cron.d: `e2scrub_all`, `sysstat`, `staticroute` (@reboot route fix). cron.daily/hourly/weekly all stock.
- **17 systemd timers**, all stock (apt-daily, logrotate, fstrim, sysstat, fwupd-refresh, man-db, e2scrub, dpkg-db-backup, etc.). `ua-timer` and `apport-autoreport` inactive.

### Other Security Posture
- **No host IDS/AV:** rkhunter, chkrootkit, aide, clamav, **auditd all NOT installed**. **AppArmor installed + active** (enforce profiles for man, snap-confine, etc.).
- **No suspicious processes:** nothing executing from `/tmp`, `/dev/shm`, or `/var/tmp`. Top processes are legitimate (node/next-server app, nginx, postgres). No unexpected listeners.
- **aaPanel admin exposure:** UI on **:10873** (SSL enabled, custom admin entry path set — both good) but **no IP allowlist (`limitip.conf` absent), no HTTP BasicAuth, no domain binding** → panel login page is reachable by raw IP from anywhere on the internet. Port **888** (phpMyAdmin/default nginx vhost) is also world-open. Both rely solely on app-layer auth.

### SECURITY POSTURE — Prioritized

**HIGH**
1. **Password + root SSH login enabled while under active brute-force, with no fail2ban.** `PermitRootLogin yes` + effective `PasswordAuthentication yes` (50-cloud-init drop-in overrides the 60- hardening file) + root has a real password + ~12k failed attempts/day + empty aaPanel ban list. This is a direct credential-stuffing target. Fix: set `PasswordAuthentication no` (resolve the drop-in ordering conflict), `PermitRootLogin prohibit-password`, install fail2ban (or populate aaPanel SSH protection), and add `AllowUsers`.
2. **Pending reboot for 18 kernel revisions, no auto-reboot, no Livepatch.** Running `-106` with `-124` installed and the reboot-required flag set for 37 days. Schedule a maintenance reboot; without Ubuntu Pro/Livepatch the only way to apply kernel CVEs is a reboot.

**MEDIUM**
3. **aaPanel admin UI (:10873) and :888 world-open with no IP allowlist / BasicAuth / domain binding.** Restrict panel access to known IPs (aaPanel "Authorized IP" / UFW source restriction) and consider closing 888 if phpMyAdmin isn't needed.
4. **Per-minute root auto-deploy cron scripts** (`lucifer-autodeploy.sh`, `lucifer-staging-autodeploy.sh`) — root-level automation triggered by git refs; audit script contents/permissions for injection paths.
5. **No host-level monitoring/IDS** (no auditd/rkhunter/AIDE/AV). Reduced detection capability if a breach occurs.

**LOW**
6. **UFW opens 5432 though Postgres binds loopback-only** — needless rule, no real exposure; remove for clarity.
7. **pure-ftpd listening publicly with TLS only optional**, though it has zero accounts — either enforce TLS (`TLS 2`) or stop the service and close 20/21/39000-40000.
8. **Two identical-comment `claude-code` SSH keys** in root authorized_keys — verify both are intended/owned.
9. **X11Forwarding yes** on a headless server — disable.

**Relevant paths:** `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/50-cloud-init.conf` & `/60-cloudimg-settings.conf` (conflicting PasswordAuthentication), `/var/run/reboot-required`, `/etc/cron.d/lucifer-autodeploy` + `/etc/cron.d/lucifer-staging-autodeploy` + `/usr/local/bin/lucifer-*-autodeploy.sh`, `/www/server/pure-ftpd/etc/pure-ftpd.conf`, `/etc/powerdns/pdns.conf` + `/etc/powerdns/named.conf`, `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys`.

### 6.6 Deploy flow (DEPLOY.md §9 — manual)
```
git pull
cd backend && npm ci && npx prisma migrate deploy && npm run build   # tsc → dist/
cd ../frontend && npm ci && npm run rebuild                          # rm -rf .next && next build
pm2 restart ecosystem.config.js                                     # ← BROKEN (see 6.2)
```
- **Prod:** branch `main`, `/www/wwwroot/Lucifersdiary/lucifers-diary` → restart `lucifer-api`/`lucifer-web`.
- **Staging:** branch `develop`, `/www/wwwroot/lucifersdiary-staging/lucifers-diary` → `…-staging`.
- Also driven automatically by the **per-minute autodeploy crons** (§1).

**Deploy-flow risks:** (1) the `pm2 restart ecosystem.config.js` step is wrong — restart by name instead; (2) **boot-time migration gate** — `&&` means a failed/locked migration takes the whole API offline (502) rather than starting degraded, and migrations run on **every** restart/reboot/resurrect; (3) no PORT pinned for prod web (relies on `next start` defaulting to 3000).
